scenarios.title: Two-condition t contrast, one run
notes: Two-step entry: Nilearn's `fit(img, events=...)` takes images directly; fmrimod needs `fmri_dataset(img, mask=, tr=, events=)` before `fmri_lm`. Candidate: let `fmri_lm(spec, img, tr=, events=, mask=)` build the dataset.

Condition contrasts need one `condition(level, term=...)` value per side plus an import; Nilearn accepts the string `'face - house'`, which `FmriLm.contrast` rejects (`KeyError: Unknown contrast name`). Candidate: parse level expressions against `DesignColumns`.
`drift('cosine')` raises without `cutoff=` and no drift is fitted unless the spec asks; Nilearn defaults to a 100 s cosine high-pass. Candidate: a documented default cutoff (SPM's 128 s).
Default noise model differs: Nilearn `FirstLevelModel` is AR(1) by default, fmrimod `fmri_lm` is OLS (aligned here with a parity knob). Worth stating in the `fmri_lm` docstring.
Default sampling grid is the TR midpoint (`slice_timing_offset=TR/2`); Nilearn/SPM/FitLins use frame start. Any cross-tool comparison needs `slice_timing_offset=0.0`.

scenarios.title: Three runs + six motion confounds, fixed effects
notes: Bug: `fmri_dataset(imgs, events=[df_run1, df_run2, ...])` is accepted, but `fmri_lm` then fails with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'columns'`. Users must merge events into one table with a `run` column; Nilearn takes the per-run list.

Confounds have no dataset slot: per-run tables must be concatenated and their names re-listed (`confounds(*motion.columns, source=motion)`); Nilearn takes `confounds=[df, ...]`. Candidate: `fmri_dataset(..., confounds=[...])` and `confounds()` defaulting to every column.

scenarios.title: Parametric modulation by reaction time
notes: Modulators are expanded per condition, so a main RT effect needs one `condition(level, term='trial_type:rt')` per level; there is no pooled-modulator spelling. Nilearn needs a hand-built duplicated event table with a `modulation` column instead, so this is roughly even.

scenarios.title: FIR basis, F over one condition's delays
notes: `hrf(..., basis='fir', nbasis=N)` keeps a 24 s span whatever N is, so N bins are not N scans. Matching Nilearn's `fir_delays=range(N)` requires importing `fmrimod.hrf.hrf_fir_generator(nbasis=N, span=N * tr)`. Candidate: `span=` (or `delays=` in scans) on `hrf()`.

`condition('face', term=...)` raises `DesignProvenanceError` (ambiguous across basis columns) on a multi-basis term; the omnibus spelling `OmnibusContrast(term=, levels=('face',))` is the one that works, and it is not discoverable from the error message.

scenarios.title: Build and inspect a design matrix without data
notes: No one-call 'spec + events + n_scans -> named design DataFrame'. `spec.compile` returns `(EventModel, BaselineModel)` separately; `EventModel.to_dataframe()` is indexed by seconds while the baseline is positional, so a naive `pd.concat(axis=1)` silently produces 240 misaligned rows instead of 160. Candidate: `fm.design_frame(spec, events, n_scans=, tr=)`.
Column names repeat the term (`trial_type_trial_type.face`, `base_cosine1_block_1`) where Nilearn uses `face`, `drift_1`.
